subject: Q3 capacity commit recommendation — usage signals & ROI recap
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@atlasai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planning Q3 commit — predictability for inference workloads

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're trying to finalize our Q3 budget and want to understand whether our current Redwood commit will be sufficient as we scale production. A few quick data points from our side:
- Current average monthly token consumption: ~820M
- Peak month last quarter: ~1.05B (driven by a marketing campaign in Feb)
- Performance needs: 95th pct latency target ~120ms for chat endpoints

Can you share any trend analysis you have and a recommendation on whether we should increase committed tokens or move to a different mix (e.g., higher commit + reserved capacity for bursts)? Also, does Redwood provide any guidance on the unit economics / discount tiers for higher commits?

Appreciate the help — cc'ing our infra lead if you need capacity details.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Zhou
VP Product
Atlas AI

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@atlasai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning Q3 commit — predictability for inference workloads

Hi Claire — thanks for the data. I pulled a short signal analysis from your account and sketched a recommended commit and terms below. Attaching a short ROI recap and the raw Q2 export.

Summary of signals (Q1–Q2):
- Avg monthly consumption (last 3 months): 820M tokens/month
- Trailing 90-day growth rate: +13% month-over-month (driven by higher inference volume in Feb)
- Peak monthly observed: 1.05B tokens
- 95th percentile latency (chat-prod): 118ms (within your stated target)
- Cache hit rate (prefix caching): 18% on average — opportunity to optimize prompts to increase this and lower token bill

Recommendation (risk-balanced):
1) Commit: increase monthly committed tokens to 1.0B (from current 600M). Rationale: covers regular demand + 5–10% buffer for organic growth; reduces on-demand overruns.
2) Reserved burst capacity: add a small Dedicated buffer (equivalent to ~150–200M tokens of capacity) that can be used for sustained peaks — this is billed as reserved throughput rather than tokens and reduces latency variance during spikes.
3) Pricing: with a 12-month commit at 1.0B/mo, we can offer a committed rate of $7.80 per 1M tokens (vs on-demand $11.50 per 1M). Estimated monthly cost under the new commit: ~$7,800 (committed baseline) + overage as applicable.

Estimated ROI (conservative):
- If you convert current actuals (avg 820M) onto the committed pricing, you save ~32% on token spend vs current on-demand.
- Break-even uplift: if your token usage grows >6% month-over-month, the commit pays off earlier because committed unit price is significantly lower.

Operational notes:
- We will add automatic fallback to a compatible, smaller model variant for non-critical routes to avoid overages during sustained surges (optional — needs QA).
- We recommend a quick prompt-refactor sprint to target a 5–8% reduction in token usage via caching and truncation — I can loop in our Optimize team to help with a 2-week run.

Next steps:
- If this looks good, we'll draft a short amendment (12-month, 1.0B/mo committed tokens + reserved burst) and send for signature.
- If you'd prefer a quarterly review cadence, we can do a 3-month pilot at a 900M commit then auto-adjust.

Attachments: Q2-usage-export.csv, Q2-roi-recap.pdf

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Quick internal note before we finalize the proposal:
- Legal will want a short SLA paragraph for availability (we usually offer 99.5% uptime for Dedicated plus credit schedule). Can we put a one-line SLA in the amendment and a path to escalate to Dedicated if they need stricter guarantees?
- Suggest adding a canary / fallback clause: if model X (production) shows >5% quality regression post-rollout, traffic can be shifted automatically to the verified baseline model for 24–72 hours with no penalty. This protects Atlas during model changes.
- On price: the $7.80/1M looks fine, but consider offering a 2% additional discount if they sign within two weeks and commit to a technical optimization project (prompt refactor + caching sprint).

Laura — can you draft the amendment with those two clauses and a short summary table of monthly economics?

Thanks,
Marcus
Revenue Operations Lead
